0 Introduction
In this revision of ISO/R 594 first published in 1967, the opportunity has been taken to incorporate test methods for gauging and performance. It should be noted that the annex does not form an integral part of the standard. IS0 664/Z deals with lock fittings.

NOTE - It is not practicable to define the characteristics of rigid or semi-ri@i materlsh with preciskm, but glass and metal may be considered as typical rigid msterielt. By contrast, many plastic materials may be regarded as semi-rigid although the wall thickness is an importsnt fatter inftuencing the rigidity of a component.

2 References
IS0 58412, Conic81 fittihgs with 8 6 % (Luerl taper for syringes, needles and certain other medical equipment - Pert 2: Lock fittings. 1) IS0 7666, Stenle hypodermic syringes for single use.

1

Scope and field of application

This part of IS0 584 specifies requirements for conical fittings
with a 6 % (Luer) taper for use with hypodermic syringes and needles and with certain other apparatus for medical use such as transfusion and infusion sets. It covers conical fittings made of rigid and of semi-rigid materials and includes test methods for gauging and performance. It excludes provision for more flexible or elastomeric materials. Figure 1 illustrates typical male 6 % (Luerl conical fitting Mrale fitting") and female 6 % (Luer) conical fitting ("female fitting").

3 Dimensions
The dimensions of male and female conical fittings shall be as given in the table and as shown in figure 1. A typical assembly of 6 % (Luer) conical fittings is shown in figure 2. The dimensions of the assembly shall be as given in the table.

4 Requirements
4.1 Gauging
When tested in accordance with 5.1, the conical fitting shall satish/ the requirements specified in 4.1.1 and 4.1.2. 4.1.1 The small end of the male conical fitting shall lie betwean thetwolimiiplanesofthegaugeandthelargerendofthetapered portion shall extend beyond the datum plane of the gauge. Rocking shall not be evident between the gauge and the fitting made of rigid11 material undergoing test. 4.1.2 The plane of the maximum diameter at the opening of the female conical fitting `shall Iii between the two kmit planas of the gauge. Rocking shall not be evident between the gauge and the fitting made of rigid 1) material undergoing test.

The axis of the conical fitting under test shall be horizontal.

4.3 Air leakage
Continued formation of air bubbles shall not be evident under the test conditions described in 5.3. Bubbles formad during the first 5 s shall be ignored.

4.4 Separation force
The conical fitting under tast shall remain attached to the test fixture, under tha test con&ions described in 5.4.

4.5 Stress cracking
There shall be no evidence of stress cracking of the conical fitting, under the test condiiions described in 5.5.
NOTE - Materiafa used for conical fittings should be resistant to stress

4.2 Liquid leakage
There shall be no leakage sufficient to form a falling drop of

water under the test conditions described in 5.2.

cracking in snvironrnents likdy to be encountered in use (for example when in contsct with alcohols).

5 Test methods
5.1 Gauging test The procedure shall be carried out as'specified in 5.1 .I to 5.1.4.
5.V.l Carry out the test using steel gauges as Wstrated in figure 3. 5.1.2 Carry out the test at a temperature of (20 f 51 OC. condition products made from

5.3.1.2 Connect the reference female fitting by means of a
leakproof joint of minimal volume to a syringe, the latter having previously passed the test for leakage past the piston during aspiration, in accordance with IS0 7886. 5.3.1.3 Draw into the syringe, through the device and the female reference fitting, a volume of recently boiled and cooled water exceeding 25 % of the graduated capacity of the syringe. 5.3.1.4 Expel the air except for a small residual air bubble.

5.1.3 Prior to testing,

, hygroscopic materials at (20 f 5) OC and (50 f lo) % relative
humidby for not less than 24 h. Conditioning is not required for products made from non-hygroscopic materials. 5.1,4 Apply the gauge to the conical fitting with a total axial force of 5 N, without the use of torque. Remove the axial load.

5.3.1.5 Adjust the volume of water in the syringe to 25 % of the graduated capacity.

5.3.1.6 Occlude the device below the conical fitting assembly. 5-3.1.7 pith the nozzle of the syringe downwards, withdraw the plunger to nominal capacity. Hold for 15 s.
5.3.2 Female fittings Conduct the test as for 5.3.1 but using a syringe with a steel male reference fitting in accordance with figure 5 to mate with the female fitting under test.
NOTE - Other test methods (e.g. involving automatic testing) may be used if good correlation is shown with the reference test specified

5.2 Test method for liquid leakage from the cohical fitting assembly under pressure
The procedure shall be carried out as specified in 5.2.1 to 5.2.6. 5.2.1 Connect the conical fitting to be tested to a steel male or female reference fitting, the dimensions of which are in accordance with those shown in figure 4 or 5, as appropriate, both components being dry. Assemble the components by ap plying an axial force of 27.5 N for 5 s whilst applying a twisting action to a value of torque not exceeding 0,l N.m to give a rotaition not exceeding 900. 5.22 Introduce water into the assemblv.

above.

5.4 Test method for separation force of conical fitting assembly
The procedure shall be carried out as specified in 5.4.1 and 5.4.2.

5.2.3 Expel air.
5.2.4 dry. Ensure that the outside of the conical fhting assembly is

Assemble as for liquid leakage testing in 5.2.

5.2.9 Seal the assembly outlet and bring the internal water pressure to an effective pressure of 300 kPa. 5.2.6 Maintain the pressure for 30 s.

5.4.2 Apply an axial force of 25 N in a direction away from the test fixture at a rate of approximately 10 N/s for a period of not less than 10 s.
